issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Meal class (and reference Meal throughout), but the template repository contains an Order class and an empty Meal.java. This mismatch (Order vs Meal) is structural and will confuse students about which class to implement and use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the problem statement: provide a proper Meal class in the template (or rename Order.java to Meal.java and update any references). Remove or clarify the Order class to avoid duplication. Ensure Main and other template references use Meal so students implement the expected class structure.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution use a class named 'Meal' to represent a meal (with name and ingredients), but the template repository provides an 'Order' class with the same structure while the template's Meal.java is empty. This creates a naming mismatch that will confuse students mapping the problem requirements (which reference Meal) to the provided template code (which exposes Order).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template use the same identifier as the problem/spec: either implement/restore Meal.java in the template (and remove or rename the duplicate Order.java), or rename Order.java to Meal.java so the class name matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure getters and the constructor match the Meal definition used in the problem.
